label: prop:markov-stabilisation-needs-a-fresh-generator
title: Markov stabilisation at the interface requires a generator the word does not already use
html:
Proposition. Let \mathbf{A} be a ring carrying a Hecke generator \sigma with \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1, and let \mathrm{tr} be linear with \mathrm{tr}(1) = 1. If \mathrm{tr}(\sigma) = z and Markov stabilisation \mathrm{tr}(W\sigma) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(W) is assumed at W = \sigma, then

  z^2 = h\,z + 1 .

Under convention D, where z = q^3/(q^2+1) and h = q - q^{-1}, that equation has no solution: for every q > 0

  z^2 - h\,z - 1
    \;=\; -\,\frac{(q^2 - q + 1)(q^2 + q + 1)}{(q^2+1)^2}
    \;<\; 0 .

Hence stabilisation fails at a generator the word already uses.

The interface between two nucleons contributes to the Markov trace through a single element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} of the two-dimensional subalgebra that \sigma generates, and the trace sees it only through the scalar \mu = a\,z + b. That collapse is not unconditional. It rests on Markov stabilisation, which the formalisation carries as a hypothesis standing in for Jones' theorem rather than as something proved in place.

The proposition settles when that hypothesis may be invoked. Taking the word to be \sigma itself — the interface generator occurring a second time — the Hecke quadratic evaluates the left-hand side outright, and stabilisation collapses into a condition on z alone. Convention D's Markov parameter misses it, and misses it by a quantity whose closed form factors into two positive-definite quadratics, q^2 \pm q + 1 = (q \pm \tfrac12)^2 + \tfrac34. The defect is therefore strictly negative at every q, not merely at the substrate value; no choice of pin recovers the identity.

The consequence is a condition on the braid word rather than on the algebra. The interface scalar \mu is available exactly when the interface generator appears once. Every canonical light-nucleus word satisfies this — the deuteron and tritium use their interface generator at index 2, helium-3 and helium-4 at index 5, one occurrence each — so the collapse holds where the framework applies it. What the proposition excludes is the assumption that it would keep holding on a word built to reuse that generator.

Scope. This is a structural exclusion, and the invariant is the closed form above rather than a numerical near-miss. It constrains the shape of the word, not the choice of interface element: an element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} remains free, and nothing here bears on which one a derivation should select.
